Funding for better connections in Kaikōura
news.body:
Locals and visitors will benefit from improved access in central Kaikōura, with the Government providing a grant of up to $500,000 from the Regional Infrastructure Fund for new facilities, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones and Tourism Minister Louise Upston say.

Kaikōura District Council will contribute $250,000 towards the $750,000 project, which will improve links between the West End, town centre, visitor facilities and the wider walking and cycling network, including the Whale Trail.

The project comprise a new pedestrian and cycle bridge across Lyell Creek and an extension of the West End car park

“Kaikōura is a tourism success story, and we need to make sure its infrastructure keeps pace. Better access around the town centre will improve the experience for visitors while making it easier for locals to get where they need to go,” Ms Upston says.

“Improving parking and walking and cycling links will make it easier to get around town and help local businesses make the most of the visitors Kaikōura attracts.”

The car park extension is expected to add around 60 spaces, alongside a new access road, footpath and recreational green space. The pedestrian and cycle bridge across Lyell Creek will provide a more direct link between the West End, town centre and wider walking and cycling network.

“This is exactly the sort of targeted regional infrastructure the Regional Infrastructure Fund is designed to support. It meets a practical local need and will make Kaikōura a better-connected place to live, visit and do business,” Mr Jones says.

The project will now progress through detailed design, costing, consenting and procurement before construction can begin.

Milford Tourism concession in place for summer
news.body:
A new concession agreement with Milford Sound Tourism Limited has now been signed – bringing certainty for the iconic tourism destination ahead of summer, Conservation Minister Tama Potaka says.

The concession enables Milford Sound Tourism Limited (MSTL) to continue managing the Piopiotahi Milford Sound visitor terminal and Freshwater Basin carparks through to 2050.

“I’m pleased to announce the completion of this process ensuring the long-term operation of important visitor infrastructure in time to support a predicted record tourism season for Piopiotahi,” says Mr Potaka.

“September cruise boat passenger numbers show an 18% increase so far this financial year compared to last year.”

“Milford Sound Tourism Limited has operated in the area for several decades. It established a shareholder partnership with Ngāi Tahu in 2025 acknowledging the deep cultural significance of Piopiotahi Milford Sound.”

In December 2025 Minister Potaka decided to grant a long-term concession for the operation of key visitor infrastructure at Milford Sound Piopiotahi, subject to terms and conditions being negotiated over the following months.

“Since I made the decision to renew this concession in December last year, DOC has been in discussions with MSTL, Ngāi Tahu, and vessel operators to understand and, where possible, address concerns regarding the operation of the facilities by MSTL.

“Through this engagement DOC developed a set of terms and conditions that are workable and address key matters such as asset management, recognising cultural values, and ensuring robust health and safety and environmental compliance.

“The new concession will provide greater transparency around maintenance and investment plans, to ensure a high-quality visitor experience. It also establishes an operator forum to encourage more proactive and coordinated tourism operations.”

The decision builds on the Government’s wider commitment to conservation and tourism in the Milford corridor, including an $8.2 million investment from the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy.

“This is an exciting time for tourism to Piopiotahi Milford Sound with a suite of DOC visitor upgrades also on track for summer,” Mr Potaka says.

“These include a new Chasm experience, a new swing bridge and track upgrades at Hinepipiwai Lake Marian Track, and a new recreational boat ramp and toilets at Deepwater Basin.”

Geothermal exploration for Taranaki and Waikato
news.body:
Two Māori-led early exploration projects in Taranaki and South Waikato could unlock new geothermal opportunities beyond New Zealand’s established geothermal areas, supporting regional growth and making greater use of home-grown energy resources, Regional Development and Resources Minister Shane Jones says.

A project exploring low-temperature geothermal resources in Taranaki will receive a $3 million grant from the Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF), while a further $2.95m grant will be used to explore the South Mangakino geothermal resource in Waikato.

“New Zealand has a long and successful history of geothermal development, primarily concentrated in the Taupō Volcanic Zone and Northland,” Mr Jones says.

“With our geology and world-class expertise, we are exceptionally well placed to make more of geothermal. Exploring more widely in places such as Taranaki and South Waikato will help build a better picture of our geothermal potential and where it could support future regional growth.

The Taranaki Geoheat Demonstrator project, led by Parininihi ki Waitōtara Incorporation, will drill two shallow test wells in the Matemateāonga Formation to improve our understanding of low-temperature geothermal heat and its potential for direct-use applications.

“Unlike the high-temperature resources traditionally associated with geothermal electricity generation, lower-temperature resources could potentially support a range of direct heat uses. Understanding where these resources exist and their characteristics is an important first step towards identifying future development and decarbonisation opportunities,” Mr Jones says.

At South Mangakino, geoscience investigations and a test well led by Wairarapa Moana ki Pouākani Incorporation will explore a geothermal anomaly beneath their Māori freehold land and provide better information about the resource. Any future development will depend on what the exploration finds, alongside further investment and consenting.

“New exploration is only part of the picture. Our From the Ground Up geothermal strategy identified an opportunity to bring data together in one accessible national database. A further $3 million has been set aside from the RIF to progress this work.

“A geothermal database can pull together existing, but fragmented data to support a better understanding of geothermal resources, derisking exploration activity, and supporting development opportunities, promoting regional growth and energy resilience in areas with geothermal resources.

“Together, these initiatives are about more than finding new geothermal resources. They are about helping our regions turn what lies beneath our feet into investment, jobs and long-term economic opportunity.” Mr Jones says.

Wairarapa grain storage set to benefit farmers
news.body:
Wairarapa farmers and allied contractors will reap the benefits of a $1.55 million loan from the Regional Infrastructure Fund to support the establishment of a new grain drying and storage facility in Carterton.

The loan will enable farmers to store up to 4000 tonnes of grain in the region instead of trucking it to Manawatu for storage, Associate Regional Development Minister Mark Patterson says.

The creation of the facility will help support more than 300 workers across farming, transport, contracting and advisory services in the region.

“A large locally based facility will improve costs, efficiencies, and resilience for both grain producers and local farmers who rely on the grain for stock feed.

“Growers have had to store excess grain outside the region, which increases costs and reduces margins for both producers and contractors,.

“This has been compounded by rising diesel prices piling on the costs of transporting grain elsewhere for storage and then back again when needed. This investment restores essential infrastructure and keeps more value in Wairarapa.”

A scalable grain-drying and storage facility is more viable and affordable for Wairarapa growers than the storage, seed-cleaning and processing facilities initially proposed, Mr Patterson says.

“Wairarapa farmers will benefit from a new seed-cleaning and processing facility in central Hawke’s Bay that the Government is also supporting with a $3 million RIF loan.”

The funding is subject to the establishment of a grower-led company to build and run the facility, provision of at least $800,000 of grower equity, and suitable site, delivery, consenting and financial arrangements.

Foxton wetland restoration backed by RIF
news.body:
The restoration and development of Piriharakeke, the river loop at Foxton, will be supported by a grant of up to $3 million from the Regional Infrastructure Fund, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones says.

“Piriharakeke is a waterway of deep significance to local hapū of Ngāti Raukawa and the wider Foxton community," Mr Jones says.

“Historically, Piriharakeke was an important mahinga kai where Māori gathered food and, later, a key transport corridor supporting the Port of Foxton.

“Over the past century, changes to the wider Manawatū River system have contributed to the decline of the river loop, degrading its environmental health and limiting community use.”

Proposed works to enhance the health of Piriharakeke include new walkways, jetties and boardwalks, improved access to the river, native planting, dredging, and other environmental improvements.

“This investment will help restore the health of the river, reconnect people with the awa, and create further opportunities for recreation, tourism and Māori enterprise while building on years of local effort to revitalise this important community asset," Mr Jones says.

The project forms Phase 3 of a broader programme of Crown-supported investment in Foxton's revitalisation over the past 10 years.

It will be delivered through a partnership involving Save Our River Trust, Ngāti Raukawa, Horowhenua District Council and other local stakeholders. Save Our River Trust will continue to play a governance role, while Horowhenua District Council will lead project delivery.

“By supporting the next phase of this project, we are helping restore a treasured local asset and leave lasting benefits for future generations," Mr Jones says

news.title: Regional radio strengthened for emergencies
news.body:
The Government is investing in the resilience of independent radio broadcasters to help ensure regional communities can access vital emergency information when electricity, internet or telecommunications services are disrupted.

Regional Development Minister Shane Jones and Emergency Management and Recovery Minister Mark Mitchell today announced a $300,000 grant from the Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF) to support the Regional Emergency Broadcasting programme.

“Regional radio stations play a vital role in keeping communities informed, particularly when other communication channels fail,” Mr Jones says.

“This RIF investment will strengthen critical communications infrastructure and help ensure New Zealanders can continue to access important information when they need it most.”

The funding will support the installation of back-up generators and associated infrastructure at 10 independently owned regional radio stations throughout the country.

Mr Mitchell says having reliable communication in regional areas is essential during emergencies, and the Regional Emergency Broadcasting programme complements Radio New Zealand’s role as the nationwide emergency radio station network.

“When events disrupt power and telecommunications networks, radio can be one of the most dependable ways for people to receive warnings and updates,” Mr Mitchell says.

“This investment will help communities remain connected to their trusted sources of information during emergencies, supporting response and recovery efforts and improving public safety.”

The work will be co-ordinated by the Independent Media Association in partnership with participating regional broadcasters. The funding will support back-up generation capability, electrical works, fuel storage, site preparation, testing and commissioning. A further $20,000 of co-funding will support project delivery.

Editors’ note

The 10 participating stations are:

Coromandel FM 1XX (Eastern Bay of Plenty) Lake FM (Taupō) Peak FM (Ruapehu District) Central FM (Central Hawke’s Bay) Beach FM 106.3 (Kapiti Coast) Compass FM (North Canterbury) Coast FM (West Coast) South Canterbury 100.3 Radio Central (Central Otago)

news.title: Government backs regional airline Air Napier
news.body:
The Government is continuing its support for regional air services, with Regional Development Minister Shane Jones and Associate Transport Minister James Meager announcing an $845,000 loan to Hawke’s Bay airline Air Napier.

The Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF) loan will help Air Napier undertake essential upgrades to its fleet and refinance some existing debt.

“Air Napier plays an important role in supporting businesses across Hawke’s Bay and Tairāwhiti, and helping people access essential services,” Mr Jones says.

“For decades, it has provided flights for Hastings-based doctors and nurses travelling to and from Wairoa, saving hours of road travel and helping ensure local communities can access vital healthcare.”

The loan is from the remainder of the Government’s $30 million regional air connectivity package, established in 2025 to support vulnerable regional air services. Air Napier is the final airline to receive support through the package.

“Regional airlines are critical to the economic success of our regions,” Mr Meager says.

“They support tourism, trade and business activity, while also helping maintain essential services during emergencies and civil defence responses.

“During Cyclone Gabrielle, Air Napier helped transport civil defence personnel, medical staff, patients, and urgent supplies, including medicines, up and down the East Coast.”

Mr Meager says regional airlines continue to face significant cost pressures in a challenging operating environment.

“The Government recognises the important role these airlines play in connecting regional communities. That is why we have continued to support the sector, including through the recent announcement of $5.7 million in grants to help meet day-to-day operating costs.”

Editors’ note

For more information on the regional air connectivity RIF package, see Government backing vital regional connectivity | Beehive.govt.nz.

The following loans have been provided to date:

Air Chathams – $17.2m to refinance debt Sounds Air – $4.5m to upgrade its fleet and refinance debt Island Air – $252,000 for fleet maintenance Golden Bay Air – $1.1m to refinance debt and fund essential ongoing maintenance Stewart Island Flights – $640,000 for aircraft refurbishment Sunair – $2.08 million for potential aircraft acquisition, fleet maintenance, and debt refinancing

news.title: Govt nurturing New Zealand’s seed supply chain
news.body:
Hawke’s Bay’s arable sector is set to benefit from a $3 million Regional Infrastructure Fund loan for a new grower-led seed cleaning, processing and storage facility in Central Hawke’s Bay, Associate Regional Development Minister Mark Patterson says.

“Currently, much of the seed grown in Hawke's Bay that requires specialist cleaning and processing is sent outside the region, including to as far away as Canterbury, before it can be sold domestically or exported. This adds cost, creates inefficiencies, and reduces returns for local growers” Mr Patterson says.

Previous government investment in 2023 supported development of a seed-drying facility, with the aim of creating high-value cropping opportunities in the region.

“This new investment builds on that foundation by bringing the full seed value chain together in one location, from drying and cleaning through to processing and storage.

“It reduces the need to transport seed outside the region for processing, meaning growers can retain more value locally while improving efficiency and resilience across the sector.

“The project positions Hawke’s Bay as a key hub for high-value seed production and will help support future growth in the sector."

Central Hawke’s Bay District Council has been working with local seed growers to bring the project to fruition and has coordinated efforts on the RIF application.

The facility will provide processing infrastructure for growers and seed companies across Hawke's Bay and the wider lower North Island, increasing processing capacity outside Canterbury and strengthening domestic supply chains.

The Regional Infrastructure Fund (RIF) funding will be provided as a loan, alongside $750,000 of grower and industry co-funding.

"This investment is about backing Hawke's Bay growers with the infrastructure they need to expand production, increase exports and create long-term opportunities for the region," Mr Patterson says.

news.title: Government backing Whale Trail tourism venture
news.body:
The Government is investing up to $12 million to connect Picton to the Whale Trail cycling and walking track, Transport and Infrastructure Minister Chris Bishop and Tourism and Hospitality Minister Louise Upston say.

A proposed bridge over SH1 and the main trunk railway, together with the associated trail works, would provide a direct connection between Picton where many walkers and cyclists disembark the Cook Strait ferries, and the 170km walking and cycling trail along the South Island's northeast coast to Kaikoura.

"The climb out of Picton on SH1 for cyclists has long been acknowledged as a tricky section. They must navigate other ferry traffic which is often heavy, particularly during the holiday periods,” Mr Bishop says.

"The bridge and associated trail work would provide a safer and more direct connection between Picton and the Whale Trail, avoiding this narrow, busy and high-speed section.”

Improving the connection to Picton would complete the Whale Trail, an important step forward for the trail itself and wider tourism across the top of the South Island, Ms Upston says.

"The Whale Trail, already a popular trail with visitors and locals alike, has the potential to attract more visitors to the region, encourage longer stays, and showcase more of what Marlborough and Kaikōura have to offer," Ms Upston says.

"This project is the last part of this tourism infrastructure. Connecting the trail directly to Picton will create a more seamless experience for visitors and strengthen one of New Zealand's premier walking and cycling attractions.”

Mr Bishop says that before any decisions is made on the construction of the bridge, government needs confidence there is a deliverable solution, a clear understanding of costs, and a pathway to successful delivery.

Government support is being provided in stages with up to $1 million from the Regional Infrastructure Fund supporting the New Zealand Transport Agency to undertake bridge investigations, design and planning.

A further $4.4m from the Infrastructure Reference Group Programme will help deliver the final section of the shared walking and cycling trail connection into Picton.

Additional funding of up to $6.6m has been ring-fenced for potential bridge construction, subject to further design work and future decisions.

news.title: Government support for aged care facility
news.body:
A loan from the Regional Infrastructure Fund will help fund a much-needed new 24-bed wing at O’Conor Home for senior citizens in Westport, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones and Associate Health Minister Casey Costello say.

“Providing safe, fit-for-purpose facilities for our senior citizens is a marker of a compassionate and caring society. When older people need this type of specialist care, it should be near their family, friends and community,” Mr Jones says.

The $13.9 million new wing will see capacity at O’Conor Home increase from 68 to 92, providing an additional 10 places for residents requiring dementia care and 14 more hospital-level care beds. Approximately 25 new staff will be recruited to care for the extra residents.

Despite having a much higher proportion of people aged 65 and over than the national average, the West Coast has seen a reduction in specialist aged-care services over the past 10 years, with O’Conor Home the only provider in the Buller district.

“Increasing access to this type of specialist residential care on the West Coast will reduce pressure on the wider health system, particularly hospital services,” Ms Costello says.

“It will also see fewer older people having to go to aged care facilities outside the region. This initiative aligns with our wider aged care reforms which will give people better access to the services they need.”

The O’Conor Institute Trust Board which owns and operates O’Conor Home has also received funding for the project from Health New Zealand, Development West Coast and the wider Buller community.

The RIF loan of $2.1m will ensure the construction-ready project goes ahead as soon as possible, with detailed design and consent work already completed, and it has an anticipated completion date of August 2028.

news.title: Government backing iwi-led geothermal potential
news.body:
Funding for two iwi-led geothermal projects near Rotorua will help build the knowledge needed to better understand the Bay of Plenty’s geothermal potential, Regional Development Minister Shane Jones says.

The Regional Infrastructure Fund will provide a $3.82 million loan towards the $5.53m Ngāti Rangiteaorere geothermal exploration programme in the Tikitere-Ruahine geothermal field, northeast of Rotorua.

A $3m grant will support research into the Waimangu geothermal system, the world’s youngest, formed by the 1886 Mount Tarawera eruption.

“Rotorua has deep geothermal knowledge and capability, and geothermal is already an important part of the Bay of Plenty economy. But there is still much to learn about the region’s geothermal potential and the opportunities it could enable,” Mr Jones says.

“This early-stage work will build that understanding, while supporting Māori land-owner led stewardship and creating opportunities for specialist contractors, skills development and employment during delivery.”

The Ngāti Rangiteaorere geothermal exploration project, led by a subsidiary of the Ngāti Rangiteaorere Koromatua Council, will explore and test the geothermal resource on Ngāti Rangiteaorere land, building a clearer picture of its characteristics and potential future uses.

The Waimangu programme, led by the Ngāti Rangitihi and Tūhourangi Tribal Authority, will undertake research drilling and monitoring to improve understanding of the protected geothermal system, while safeguarding its significant environmental, cultural and tourism va­lues and generating wider public-good knowledge.

“The Government’s From the Ground Up geothermal strategy recognises that high upfront costs, uncertainty and gaps in geothermal knowledge can be barriers to exploration and research. It sets a clear direction for building science and technical capability, strengthening regional economies and supporting iwi and hapū aspirations for geothermal resources,” Mr Jones says.

“These projects put the strategy into action by building knowledge of important geothermal systems, supporting iwi-led stewardship and providing a stronger evidence base for future decisions.”

Any future development leading from the projects would depend on the results of the research and exploration, further funding and investment, regulatory and consenting requirements, and appropriate protection of environmental and cultural values.
